capture.final_message:
Use the derived series as the common mechanism.

- For the first conjunct, inherit solvability from \(G\) to the subgroup \(H\). Thus the derived series of \(H\) eventually reaches \(\bot\). Since \(H\neq\bot\), its first derived subgroup cannot equal \(H\): otherwise \([H,H]=H\) would make every subsequent term equal to \(H\), contradicting termination. As \([H,H]\le H\) always, this gives \([H,H]<H\).

- For the second conjunct, the hypothesis says \(G\) is abelian. Hence every commutator is trivial, so \([G,G]=\bot\). The derived series therefore reaches \(\bot\) after one step, proving that \(G\) is solvable.

A useful organization is to first establish subgroup-inheritance of solvability and the standard inclusion \([H,H]\le H\), then use stabilization of the derived series for the strictness argument.
